novel_mechanics_found: Level 5's small colored blocks are temporary pressure plates: a player standing on a plate removes every large barrier of the matching color, and those barriers return immediately when the plate is released. Closed barriers can surround an occupying sprite without resetting it, and fixed wall segments plus temporarily closed gates can be used as tandem-movement pins. Level 6 adds a selectable, driveable 2x2 color-9 object; it moves in 4-pixel steps, is blocked by colored plates and closed colored barriers, can be transported through an opened barrier while the players remain frozen on their plates, and works as a physical pin beneath a player. The level-6 checkerboard enclosure is an electric reset surface: touching the central seam resets both players and the movable object to the level start.
narrative: Replayed the resolver's 205-action prefix from a fresh reset and confirmed levels_completed=4. On level 5, direct contact with the unexplained small colored objects revealed temporary plate-controlled gates; I then used plate holding, barrier closure around a sprite, and fixed-wall pinning to route both sprites into the connected top corridor and coalesce them. The live win occurred at action 289, and a fresh-reset reproduce() gate on the complete 289-action sequence reached level 5 and passed. I explored level 6 through action 374 live (663 total steps including the 289-step gate): I moved its selectable color-9 object through an opened barrier, successfully used it to pin one player while the other crossed a color gate, and tested clicks, ACTION5, plate approaches, and the lower central seam. The remaining seam stayed lethal and reset all level state, so I stopped at a genuine unresolved routing wall with 37 budgeted steps unused rather than spend them on repetitions.
gotchas: Level 5 horizontal controls are reversed relative to the banked level-4 description: ACTION3 converges the sprites and ACTION4 diverges them; level 6 switches back to ACTION4 converging and ACTION3 diverging.
Level 5 plates are momentary, not collectible keys: leaving a plate restores its matching barriers immediately.
A restored colored barrier may close around a sprite already occupying its opening; the sprite remains alive and can move out, while the surrounding wall provides a useful pin.
Level 5 solution staging is lower f plate -> right c plate -> right e plate -> upper f plate -> coalescence in the open top corridor.
Level 6's 2x2 color-9 object is click-selectable (9 becomes 11 and both players become color 1); arrows then drive it in 4-pixel steps, and clicking a player returns to tandem control.
The level-6 movable object cannot occupy a colored plate and cannot pass a closed colored gate; freeze both players on the upper plates to transport it through an opened gate.
Placing the level-6 object directly below a player on an upper plate pins that player, allowing the other sprite to cross its matching open gate.
Touching the level-6 checkerboard central seam resets both player positions and returns the movable object to its initial socket, undoing the entire level setup.
Clicking level-6 plates, large colored barriers, or checkerboard cells has no observed effect; ACTION5 is also a no-op there.
